transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Noah Becker (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Seastar CTO), Arjun Singh (Seastar ML Eng), Priya Rao (Seastar PM), Leo Carter (Seastar Infosec)

Summary: initial discovery focused on model selection for multilingual customer-facing assistant, clarification of context-length needs, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private is the right fit given data residency and tool-calling requirements. Agreed to run a 1k-sample benchmark and follow up with infra deep-dive.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick things off—quick intros?
[00:22] Maya: hi i'm maya, cto at seastar, we build a multilingual customer assistant for ecommerce and travel, want to evaluate model candidates and deployment options, thanks for doing this.
[00:35] Priya: priya here, product lead for the assistant, key metrics are latency under 400ms for short queries and high fidelity in spanish and french.
[01:10] Arjun: arjun—ml engineer, we'll be focused on model accuracy and cost, also need tool-calling (booking, order lookup APIs) and safe output.
[01:35] Leo: leo from infosec, i'll watch security and residency needs; we have EU customers so data residency + KMS is important.
[02:10] Samir: great, lina and noah from our se team are here to dive into performance trade-offs, lina do you want to frame how we think about model selection at redwood?
[02:35] Lina: yeah thanks, at a high level we separate by capability: smaller open models for embeddings/fast responses, mid-size instruction-tuned for chat, large context models for long form. we evaluate context length, multilingual coverage, and tool-calling / function call support. at redwood we support hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private v p c/on-prem options.
[03:05] Noah: also worth noting infra tradeoffs—dedicated gives you predictable p99 latency and isolation, private gives KMS and full control but more ops. hosted is fastest to get started.
[04:05] Maya: can you call out specific open models you usually recommend? we've been trialing llm-3 and a couple of community weights (mistral-style) but results are mixed in french.
[04:55] Lina: sure — common candidates: llama 3 family, mistral-instruct variants, falcon 180b (heavy but good few-shot), and newer multilingual models—some community models have strong multilingual zero-shot, others need instruction tuning. we often benchmark across 2-3 variants.
[06:30] Arjun: what's the practical context-length tradeoff? we consider 32k for long conversation state but most real interactions are 1-2k tokens; however for complex orders we need 8-16k.
[07:05] Samir: that's helpful — we should match model variant to typical sequence length. for 8-16k we can use medium-large models with 16k context; for 32k you pick explicit long-context variants or chunking plus kv-cache. some models also degrade in latency as context grows.
[08:12] Priya: tool calling—we need function/structured output support to invoke booking APIs and to return structured JSON. does redwood support that on hosted?
[08:40] Lina: yes, we support streaming + structured output and function calling. implementation differs slightly per model—some models have better native function-calling patterns; our runtime provides a uniform function-calling shim so your app sees consistent behavior. there can be minor differences in how prompts are structured.
[09:12] Leo: for private deployments we need KMS for key management and audit logs; will dedicated cover that?
[09:44] Noah: dedicated provides isolation but KMS integrations and customer-managed keys are part of our private offering. we do offer KMS integration with dedicated in some enterprise plans, but the strongest control is Private (VPC/on-prem) where you control network and keys.
[10:30] Maya: latency targets—priya mentioned 400ms, is that realistic for 2-4k token flows on dedicated?
[10:58] Lina: 400ms is realistic for short prompts on optimized small-medium models. for 2-4k token context, end-to-end latency will be higher; p50 might be low but p95/p99 will grow. dedicated with optimized kernels and batching helps predictability; we can run benchmarks with your typical prompts to give exact numbers.
[12:00] Arjun: about quantization—we're interested in cost reduction; what's redwood's stance on 4-bit vs 8-bit quant? does that affect function calling reliability?
[12:35] Lina: quantization reduces memory/cost; 8-bit (or q8) is a safer default with minimal quality loss. 4-bit offers more savings but can introduce instabilities for some models. function-calling behavior can be sensitive; we recommend testing on your dataset. our optimize tooling suggests quant profiles per-model/workload.
[15:45] Priya: multilingual eval—we need strong spanish/french/portuguese support. do you have examples where one model beats others?
[16:10] Samir: in our experience, instruction-tuned Llama-3 variants and some Mistral-based intruct models do well; however, community models vary. we usually do a head-to-head with your labeled prompts.
[18:03] Maya: what about hallucinations and safety—particularly with tool calling we can't have false booking confirmations.
[18:30] Lina: we have a few levers—prompt engineering and system messages, model choice, and post-processing/verification layers. for critical actions we recommend transactional verification: model returns structured payload, then your service validates before committing. we can also add guard rails in the runtime.
[21:20] Arjun: do you support hybrid routing? e.g., route low-risk queries to hosted to save cost, and high-risk to dedicated/private?
[21:52] Noah: yes we have smart routing policies—by route, rate, or SLO. you can define fallbacks and routing by policy (latency, cost, region). if capacity is constrained we can failover to a compatible variant.
[24:10] Priya: curious about token-level billing—we want predictable cost per session. how fine-grained is the cost data?
[24:45] Samir: console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and token cost attribution by model. for Dedicated you can get quota and reserved pricing to stabilize cost.
[28:00] Leo: security checklist—SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data retention policies—do you have those docs?
[28:30] Samir: yes we'll share SOC 2 report and security FAQ. for SSO we support SAML, OIDC and role-based controls. audit logs and retention are configurable and we can map to your compliance needs.
[31:55] Maya: ok on benchmarks—we'll send a slice with multilingual queries and tool-calling examples. what's the expected turnaround on a 1k sample run?
[32:20] Lina: usually 3-5 business days to run comparative benchmarks across 3 models and return latency/cost/quality metrics. if we need infra access for private trials it could be longer.
[35:40] Arjun: one more on model ops—how is rolling updates and version pinning handled? we need reproducibility.
[36:05] Noah: you can pin model versions per-route, do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback. all of that is part of our console and API. we also keep model artifacts and kernel selection logs for reproducibility.
[39:05] Priya: any red flags we should be aware of when choosing hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[39:30] Lina: hosted is fastest and good for early testing; dedicated is the sweet spot for predictable production performance; private is for strict security/regulatory needs. consider team ops maturity and data residency. also evaluate token cost vs SLOs—sometimes dedicated with batching saves money at scale.
[42:22] Maya: sounds good—can you share a recommended shortlist for us? maybe 2-3 models with suggested deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) per use case?
[42:55] Samir: yes we'll propose: 1) Llama-3-instruct medium on Dedicated for primary assistant (balance of cost & latency), 2) Mistral-instruct variant on Hosted for bursty/prompt-heavy flows, 3) Long-context Llama-3-32k variant on Private for enterprise EU customers needing residency. we'll include quant recommendations.
[44:30] Priya: excellent. timeline—we aim to pick pilot model and deployment by end of month, and run benchmarks next week if possible.
[44:50] Samir: action items recap: samir send pricing and sizing, lina run benchmark plan, maya share dataset slice, leo share compliance list.
[46:10] Maya: thanks all, this was useful. looking forward to the benchmark.
[46:50] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the docs. bye.
